research_topic: Comparative multi-omics study of tobacco flavor fermentation mechanisms using the same tobacco variety fermented in Yunnan vs Henan, two locations with distinct altitude, temperature, and humidity patterns. The study integrates dual RNA-seq transcriptomics, dual proteomics, metabolomics, volatile flavoromics, and microbiome profiling to identify geographic and fermentation-stage-driven biological mechanisms underlying high-quality tobacco flavor formation.
disease_or_phenotype: Tobacco leaf fermentation quality phenotype, including aroma formation, flavor precursor accumulation, irritancy reduction, sugar-nicotine balance, and sensory quality improvement
organism: Tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum) leaves and their associated surface/epiphytic microbiota, including bacteria (e.g., Staphylococcus, Pseudomonas, Bacillus, Pantoea, Sphingomonas, Aspergillus) and fungi (e.g., Aspergillus, Alternaria, Penicillium, Candida, Inocybe)
tissue: Fresh and fermented tobacco leaves at multiple fermentation timepoints, including cigar tobacco leaves and flue-cured tobacco leaves

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Fermentation time is a dominant selective force shaping tobacco-associated microbial community assembly; deterministic homogeneous selection predominates during middle fermentation stages, while stochastic processes are more important at early and late stages.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: PERMANOVA attributed49.54% of bacterial community variation to fermentation time; βNTI/RCbray null models showed homogenizing dispersal/undominated processes at M0/M12 and homogeneous selection at M3/M6/M9. Communities converged at the same fermentation stage regardless of leaf position.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Microbial community succession drives stage-specific degradation of macromolecules and harmful compounds, including starch, protein, cellulose, pectin, and nicotine, producing sugars, amino acids, organic acids, ammonia, and aroma precursors.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Carbohydrate metabolism genes were enriched during early fermentation, while amino acid metabolism genes were enriched later. Enzyme activities such as alpha-amylase, neutral protease, polyphenol oxidase, and phenylalanine ammonia lyase increased significantly; total nitrogen and alkaloids decreased during fermentation.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Core bacteria and fungi have complementary functional roles in carbon-nitrogen coupling metabolism: bacteria mainly participate in amino acid and alkaloid metabolism, while fungi mainly degrade polysaccharides and promote flavonoid transformation.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Staphylococcus, Pseudomonas, and Cyanobacteria were associated with phenylalanine/tyrosine/tryptophan biosynthesis and alkaloid metabolism; Aspergillus, Penicillium, and Inocybe were associated with polysaccharide degradation, carbon skeleton formation, and increased quercetin with decreased isoguercitrin and rutin.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Bacillus is a key functional genus in tobacco flavor improvement: it secretes amylase, protease, and cellulase, participates in aromatic amino acid metabolism, and promotes production of aromatic volatile compounds.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Bacillus positively correlated with tryptophan, tyrosine, aspartic acid, phenylalanine, phenylacetaldehyde, phenol, benzyl alcohol, and coumarin. A four-Bacillus combination increased total sugar by ~14.5%, reducing sugar by ~12.7%, optimized sugar-to-nicotine ratio to9.67, and improved sensory flavor.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Microbial degradation of nicotine and alkaloids is a critical determinant of tobacco quality, reducing irritancy and altering flavor.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Pseudomonas species, Staphylococcus nepalensis, Bacillus subtilis, Alternaria alternata, and Aspergillus cristatus were shown to degrade nicotine. Nicotine content decreased from4.76% to3.62% in one fermentation study and total alkaloids decreased by26.1% in another; nicotinate/nicotinamide pathway metabolites changed significantly.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: The Maillard reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars contributes to tobacco flavor and color by generating heterocyclic compounds such as pyrazine and furan, and sugar-amino acid condensates serve as aroma precursors.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Co-fermentation with malic acid and glucose produced the highest sensory quality; glucose can react with amino acids to form sugar-amino acid condensates. Heterocyclic compounds and darkening of tobacco leaves were attributed to Maillard/caramelization reactions.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Acidic fermentation improves cigar tobacco quality by reducing free nicotine proportion, stabilizing nitrogen as NH4+, enhancing carbon/nitrogen metabolic enzyme activities, and modifying the TCA cycle and phenylalanine metabolism.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Free nicotine proportion decreased by up to46.98%; NH4+-N increased with decreasing pH; PPO, PAL, neutral protease, and alpha-amylase activities increased; differential metabolites were enriched in citrate cycle and phenylalanine metabolism, with ACO, acnB, sucD, aarC, PDHA, and PDHB showing differential abundance.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Microbial alpha-diversity trajectory is system-dependent and may reflect fermentation conditions, additives, or time scale.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: One study found reduced bacterial/KO diversity at3–9 months with rebound at12 months; another reported increased diversity after fermentation; a third found initial increase then plateau at50 days; a fourth found richness decreased first and then increased. These contrasting patterns likely depend on tobacco type, fermentation duration, and intervention.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Low-abundance or co-occurring microbial taxa can maintain community stability and contribute functionally to late fermentation, especially flavor synthesis and alkaloid degradation.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Candida accounted for only0.42% of fungal abundance but was identified as a late-fermentation biomarker and co-occurring taxon. Bioaugmentation with Candida parapsilosis or C. metapsilosis reduced total alkaloids and increased total flavor components, including carotenoid/chlorophyll degradation products or cembranoid/Maillard products.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Positive microbial interactions and network complexity are associated with better fermentation quality, while negative interactions can reflect resource competition during middle fermentation.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Exogenous additive treatments increased network edges, average degree, graph density, and clustering coefficients, with positive interactions reaching91.4% and81.8%; untreated controls had64.4% positive interactions. In another study, middle-fermentation networks had fewer edges but higher proportions of negative interactions.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Sugar content, especially total sugar, is a key regulator of microbial community assembly and volatile flavor formation; optimizing sugar-to-nicotine ratio improves sensory quality.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: PLS-SEM showed total sugar had the strongest effect on bacterial genera, a negative effect on fungal genera, and directly influenced flavor metabolites. Bacillus inoculation optimized sugar-to-nicotine ratio to near10, a previously proposed optimal value.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Flavor formation during fermentation arises largely from degradation products of tobacco precursor metabolites: carotenoids, chlorophyll, cembranoids, and Maillard reaction products.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Detected flavor components mainly included degradation products of carotenoids, Maillard reaction products, chlorophyll degradation products, and cembranoid degradation products. Neophytadiene, β-damascone, megastigmatrienone, solanone, and furan-type compounds accumulated during fermentation.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Cigar tobacco leaf fermentation is a microbially mediated carbon-nitrogen coupling process; controlling carbon-nitrogen balance is critical for flavor quality.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Carbohydrates are decomposed and consumed to supply energy and carbon skeletons, while nitrogen-containing macromolecules are degraded into volatile compounds and flavor precursors. Carbon source consumption was significantly higher than nitrogen source consumption in one multi-region study.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: Geographic and environmental factors shape initial microbial communities and metabolic outcomes; comparing regions can reveal environment-driven differences in fermentation mechanisms.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: Microbial communities vary by region, variety, and fermentation method; environmental/climatic conditions can shape dominant microbiota and metabolic outcomes. Four producing regions shared only a small set of common differential metabolites before/after fermentation, suggesting region-specific metabolic responses.

biological_mechanisms.mechanism: There is an optimal fermentation endpoint at which microbial communities and metabolite profiles stabilize; extending fermentation beyond this point may provide little benefit and could risk over-degradation of desirable flavor compounds.
biological_mechanisms.evidence: In one cigar study, T2 at50 days achieved microbial equilibrium and metabolite stabilization; extending to T3 offered minimal additional benefit and risked over-fermentation. In flue-cured tobacco aging, metabolic profiles stabilized after the second year, supporting two years as the optimal fermentation period.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Yunnan vs Henan within the same variety, timepoint, and fermentation phase
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Identify location/altitude-driven differences in microbial community assembly, gene/protein expression, metabolites, and volatile flavor compounds despite the same host variety.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Fresh leaves (phase = fresh) vs each fermentation timepoint within each location
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Define fermentation-induced changes and identify core conserved and location-specific metabolic pathways and microbial taxa.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Early vs middle vs late fermentation stages within each location
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Reveal stage-specific functional succession, such as early carbohydrate degradation, middle chemotaxis/quorum sensing/biofilm formation, and late amino acid/nicotine metabolism.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: High-altitude vs low-altitude samples across locations
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Test whether altitude-associated temperature/humidity patterns drive convergent or divergent microbial community assembly and flavor outcomes.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: High-sensory-quality vs low-sensory-quality fermentation batches or endpoints
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Identify biomarker microorganisms, genes/proteins, metabolites, and volatile compounds that distinguish high-quality flavor fermentation.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Time-course longitudinal analysis using all fermentation timepoints
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Model dynamic trajectories of multi-omics features with methods such as Mfuzz, TCAM, or spline-based clustering to identify stage-specific modules and optimal fermentation endpoints.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Microbiome-metabolome-volatilome correlation analysis (e.g., Spearman/Mantel/O2PLS/DIABLO) using shared samples
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Link dominant or keystone microbial taxa to quality-related metabolites and volatile flavor compounds, integrating bacteria and fungi separately.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Transcriptome/proteome vs metabolome pathway joint enrichment
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Identify coordinated expression changes in key pathways such as TCA cycle, phenylalanine/tyrosine/tryptophan metabolism, starch/sucrose metabolism, and nicotine degradation that drive metabolite and flavor changes.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Microbial co-occurrence network analysis by location and fermentation stage
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Detect keystone taxa and shifts from competitive to cooperative interactions; compare network stability between Yunnan and Henan conditions.

comparison_design_suggestions.comparison: Differential abundance analysis (DESeq2/edgeR/LEfSe/ANCOM-BC) on each omics layer
comparison_design_suggestions.purpose: Generate robust lists of differentially abundant genes, proteins, taxa, metabolites, and volatiles for pathway enrichment and biomarker discovery.

expected_findings: Fermentation time and geographic location will both shape microbial community structure, with location effects driven by altitude, temperature, and humidity patterns.

Core functional taxa such as Bacillus, Pseudomonas, Staphylococcus, Aspergillus, and Candida will be differentially abundant between Yunnan and Henan or across fermentation stages and will correlate with quality-related metabolites and volatiles.

Key metabolic pathways enriched across omics layers will include amino acid metabolism, TCA cycle, phenylalanine/tyrosine/tryptophan metabolism, starch/sucrose metabolism, nicotine degradation/alkaloid biosynthesis, and Maillard reaction.

Free nicotine and total alkaloids are expected to decrease during fermentation, while reducing sugars, total sugars, and sugar-nicotine ratio will shift toward values associated with improved sensory quality.
Geographic divergence will be most visible at early fermentation timepoints, with possible convergence at later timepoints due to similar selective pressures from the fermentation environment.

Multi-omics integration will identify specific microbial genera and host/microbial enzymes (e.g., alpha-amylase, glucoamylase, neutral protease, PPO, PAL, ACO, PDHA) that jointly regulate flavor precursor production.
Low-abundance taxa may act as keystone species or late-stage functional contributors despite low relative abundance, especially in stable microbial networks.

Optimal fermentation endpoints can be inferred from stabilization of microbial alpha diversity, metabolite profiles, and volatile flavor compound abundance; over-fermentation may lead to loss of desirable flavor compounds.
